sourceCheck: Verified [CKAD_Curriculum_v1.37.pdf](https://github.com/cncf/curriculum/blob/master/CKAD_Curriculum_v1.37.pdf), byte-identical to the repository's v1.35 file. The [README](https://github.com/cncf/curriculum) ties curriculum major/minor versions to Kubernetes. The [exam page](https://training.linuxfoundation.org/certification/certified-kubernetes-application-developer-ckad/) still names Kubernetes v1.37 and confirms five domains, weights 20%, 20%, 15%, 25%, 20%, and all 24 competencies. It confirms two hours, command-line performance tasks and Intermediate experience. The PDF says 'depreciations'; the exam page says 'deprecations' and places ConfigMaps before Define resource requirements. The supplied sections preserve the PDF competency order and merge neighbouring bullets. Pinned Kubernetes v1.37; [releases](https://kubernetes.io/releases/) lists latest patch 1.37.1, released 2026-09-15, and maintained branches 1.37, 1.36 and 1.35. Read the v1.35, v1.36 and v1.37 announcements, migration guide and deprecation policy. The [migration guide](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/deprecation-guide/) lists no API versions removed after v1.32; its latest removal is flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta3 in v1.32. [Helm releases](https://github.com/helm/helm/releases) shows v4.3.0 and v3.22.0; [Helm 3 support](https://helm.sh/blog/helm-v3-end-of-life/) ends bug fixes/final feature releases on 2026-09-09 and security fixes on 2027-02-10. Required section documentation and feature states were checked. Kustomize reference URLs failed, so their official repository sources were checked: [labels](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/blob/master/site/content/en/docs/Reference/API/Kustomization%20File/labels.md) confirms includeSelectors:true also adds template labels. Another scope correction: [EndpointSlices](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/endpoint-slices/) can retain unready endpoints with readiness conditions; no ready Pods does not imply an empty slice.

cards.statement: When an image reference has a tag and a digest, the kubelet uses the tag to choose the image.
cards.explanation: The kubelet pulls the image identified by the digest when a reference includes both a tag and a digest.
cards.misconception: A tag overrides a digest in a combined image reference.

cards.statement: Pinning a Deployment's image by digest keeps its new Pods on that image when a registry tag moves.
cards.explanation: An image digest identifies fixed content. Moving a registry tag leaves the content selected by the Deployment's digest unchanged.

cards.statement: For a newly created Pod using `:latest`, Kubernetes defaults an omitted imagePullPolicy to Always.
cards.explanation: At creation, the API server assigns Always when the image uses the latest tag and imagePullPolicy is omitted.

cards.statement: Changing a Deployment's image tag to `:latest` automatically changes its imagePullPolicy to Always.
cards.explanation: Kubernetes sets the default imagePullPolicy at object creation. A later image change preserves the existing policy unless you explicitly edit it.
cards.misconception: Kubernetes recalculates imagePullPolicy after an image change.

cards.statement: A Pod's imagePullSecrets can reference a registry credential Secret stored in a different namespace.
cards.explanation: A Pod's imagePullSecrets refer to Secrets in that Pod's namespace. Create the registry credential Secret in the namespace that uses it.
cards.misconception: Registry credentials can be shared through cross-namespace Secret references.

source.title: Pull an Image from a Private Registry

cards.statement: A ServiceAccount's imagePullSecrets automatically populate new Pods that use it and omit imagePullSecrets.
cards.explanation: Kubernetes copies a ServiceAccount's imagePullSecrets into a new Pod when the Pod supplies none.

cards.statement: A missing registry image can leave a container waiting with ImagePullBackOff while the kubelet retries.
cards.explanation: The kubelet retries when the registry fails to supply the requested image. ImagePullBackOff shows that container startup is waiting on a successful pull.

cards.statement: Setting a container's args alone makes the kubelet replace the image's default executable command.
cards.explanation: When you supply args and leave command unset, the kubelet runs the image's default command with your replacement arguments.
cards.misconception: Providing args overrides both the command and its arguments.

source.title: Define a Command and Arguments for a Container

cards.statement: The API server can accept changes to each container's command when you update an existing Pod.
cards.explanation: A container's command is fixed when the Pod is created. Create a replacement Pod to use a different command.
cards.misconception: A running Pod's command is an editable configuration field.

source.title: Define a Command and Arguments for a Container

cards.statement: The kubelet expands `$(VAR)` in container args using the container's environment variables.
cards.explanation: The kubelet substitutes a defined environment variable in a command or argument that uses the $(VAR) form.

source.title: Define a Command and Arguments for a Container

cards.statement: A StatefulSet controller automatically creates the headless Service named in its manifest.
cards.explanation: You create the headless Service used for a StatefulSet's network identity; the StatefulSet controller does not create it.
cards.misconception: The StatefulSet controller creates the referenced headless Service automatically.

cards.statement: A StatefulSet keeps its template-created PersistentVolumeClaims after scale-down by default.
cards.explanation: StatefulSet retention defaults to Retain, so template-created PersistentVolumeClaims survive scale-down.

cards.statement: A DaemonSet controller automatically adds a Pod when a newly joined node meets its scheduling constraints.
cards.explanation: A DaemonSet controller reconciles newly added eligible nodes by creating a Pod there.

cards.statement: A Job's `parallelism` sets the total number of successful Pods needed for each completed Job.
cards.explanation: A Job's parallelism controls concurrent execution. For a fixed-completion Job, completions sets the success count.
cards.misconception: Job parallelism specifies the total required successes rather than concurrency.

cards.statement: A Job's `activeDeadlineSeconds` stops retries even when its `backoffLimit` still permits them.
cards.explanation: A Job stops launching retries when its active deadline expires, even if its retry allowance remains.

cards.statement: Setting a Job's `suspend` to true pauses its active Pods so they resume from their current processes.
cards.explanation: Suspending a Job terminates its active Pods; resuming creates replacement Pods rather than continuing their paused processes.
cards.misconception: Job suspension pauses existing container processes for later resumption.

cards.statement: Under its default success rules, an Indexed Job waits for a successful Pod at each completion index.
cards.explanation: Under its default success rules, an Indexed Job counts multiple successful Pods with the same index as one completed index.

cards.statement: A CronJob with `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` replaces its active Job when the next scheduled run is due.
cards.explanation: With Forbid, a CronJob skips a scheduled run while its previous Job remains active, instead of replacing that Job.
cards.misconception: Forbid replaces an overlapping Job rather than skipping the new run.

cards.statement: A CronJob skips a missed run once the delay exceeds its configured `startingDeadlineSeconds`.
cards.explanation: A CronJob's startingDeadlineSeconds limits how late a missed run starts; the controller skips that occurrence after the deadline.

cards.statement: By default, a CronJob interprets its schedule in the worker node's local time zone.
cards.explanation: The kube-controller-manager uses its own local time zone for a CronJob schedule when timeZone is omitted.
cards.misconception: A CronJob takes its default schedule time zone from a worker node.

cards.statement: Two containers in one Pod can reach each other's network listeners through the shared localhost address.
cards.explanation: Containers in one Pod use the same network namespace, so localhost reaches listeners in a sibling container.

cards.statement: The kubelet can run ordinary init containers concurrently before starting the app containers.
cards.explanation: The kubelet runs ordinary init containers in sequence, waiting for one to succeed before it starts the next.
cards.misconception: Ordinary init containers run concurrently during Pod initialization.

cards.statement: By default, containers in one Pod see one another's processes through a shared process namespace.
cards.explanation: Containers use separate process namespaces by default. Set shareProcessNamespace to true when containers need to inspect one another's processes.
cards.misconception: Containers automatically share their Pod's process namespace.

cards.statement: Since Kubernetes v1.33, a running native sidecar holds a Job open after its main containers finish.
cards.explanation: A native sidecar's continued execution does not block its Job from completing after the main container finishes.
cards.misconception: A running native sidecar prevents a Job from reaching completion.

cards.statement: A container restart preserves the files stored in its Pod's emptyDir volume.
cards.explanation: The kubelet keeps an emptyDir volume across container restarts within the same Pod.

cards.statement: A container's writes to a memory-backed emptyDir count toward its ephemeral-storage limit.
cards.explanation: Files written to a memory-backed emptyDir count against the memory limit of the container that wrote them.
cards.misconception: RAM-backed emptyDir data consumes ephemeral-storage rather than the writer's memory allowance.

cards.statement: The control plane creates a generic ephemeral volume's PersistentVolumeClaim from the Pod's template.
cards.explanation: For a generic ephemeral volume, the ephemeral volume controller creates the PersistentVolumeClaim using the Pod's volumeClaimTemplate.

cards.statement: Since Kubernetes v1.36, a runtime with image volume support mounts an image volume read-only.
cards.explanation: The runtime exposes an image volume's OCI image or artifact as read-only content for mounted files.

cards.statement: A ReadWriteOnce volume can accept read-write mounts from multiple Pods on the same node.
cards.explanation: ReadWriteOnce restricts read-write mounting to one node, so Pods sharing that node can use the same volume.

cards.statement: Setting a PersistentVolumeClaim's `storageClassName` to an empty string selects the default StorageClass.
cards.explanation: An empty storageClassName requests storage with no class. Omitting the field permits default StorageClass selection.
cards.misconception: An empty storageClassName selects the default StorageClass.

cards.statement: Scaling a Deployment with `kubectl scale` makes its controller record a new rollout revision.
cards.explanation: A Deployment records a revision for a Pod template change. Changing the desired replica count leaves its rollout revision unchanged.
cards.misconception: Scaling a Deployment counts as a rollout.

cards.statement: You can change an existing Deployment's label selector through `kubectl apply` with an updated manifest.
cards.explanation: The API server rejects changes to an existing Deployment's label selector. Changing that selector requires replacing the Deployment.
cards.misconception: Applying a new manifest updates a Deployment's selector.

cards.statement: During a Recreate rollout, the Deployment controller stops the old Pods before it creates replacements.
cards.explanation: Recreate terminates the previous revision's Pods before starting the new revision, leaving a gap in application availability.

cards.statement: For a rolling update, maxSurge sets how many desired replicas the Deployment controller can leave unavailable.
cards.explanation: maxSurge gives a rolling update room to create Pods above the desired replica count.
cards.misconception: maxSurge measures unavailable replicas during an update.

cards.statement: `kubectl rollout status` watches a Deployment's rollout until it finishes by default.
cards.explanation: kubectl rollout status follows rollout progress. It keeps watching the latest rollout if another begins during the watch.

cards.statement: `kubectl rollout undo` can restore a Deployment's Pod template from a particular retained revision.
cards.explanation: kubectl rollout undo accepts a chosen revision from the retained rollout history, allowing recovery to an earlier Pod template.

cards.statement: `kubectl rollout pause` makes the Deployment controller stop the containers in its running Pods.
cards.explanation: Pausing a Deployment holds back rollouts from Pod template updates. Existing Pods keep running while the Deployment is paused.
cards.misconception: Pausing a rollout suspends the application's running containers.

cards.statement: The Deployment controller automatically rolls back a stalled rollout when progressDeadlineSeconds expires.
cards.explanation: The controller reports Progressing=False with reason ProgressDeadlineExceeded after the deadline. Kubernetes reports the stall and leaves rollback to you or another orchestrator.
cards.misconception: The rollout progress deadline triggers automatic recovery.

cards.statement: You can switch blue/green traffic between two Deployments by changing the frontend Service's selector.
cards.explanation: A frontend Service selects the active version's Pods. Switching that selector directs new traffic to the other prepared Deployment.

source.title: Zero-downtime Deployment in Kubernetes with Jenkins

cards.statement: With default Service routing to both versions, canary traffic roughly follows the ready Pod replica ratio.
cards.explanation: With a Service balancing across ready Pods from both Deployments, adjusting their replica ratio changes the approximate canary traffic share.

source.title: Deploy a Release Using a Canary Deployment
